fields.description:
## Problem

The MCP server's code workspace is cloned once and then never updated, so every gate it runs reads a frozen tree that drifts further from `main` every day.

The workspace is the docker volume `gerrit_mcp_code`, mounted into the MCP container at `/var/gerrit/site/mcp-code` and passed as both `MCP_CODE_DIR` and `REBAR_ROOT` (`infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:390-417`). `REBAR_ROOT` is the tree the completion-verifier and plan-review gates inspect when they check whether work is present in the repository.

`infra/scripts/mcp-entrypoint.sh` clones that directory only when it is missing or its `HEAD` does not resolve (`mcp-entrypoint.sh:127-130`), cloning `main` bloblessly at `155-164`; `provision_code()` returns immediately for any checkout that is merely present (`175-181`). There is no `fetch` and no `merge --ff-only` on an existing valid checkout. `autodeploy.sh` only mounts the volume; it never touches the checkout inside it. So once the clone succeeds, nothing in the system ever advances it again.

## Evidence

Observed on the prod host `i-00880b2c7f13527c5` on 2026-09-17:

- `gerrit_mcp_code` was on branch `main` at `665d1d0480`, clean, **130 commits behind** `origin/main`.
- Its reflog shows a `merge origin/main: Fast-forward` on 2026-09-07 23:36 and a `clone` on 2026-08-27, and nothing since. The 09-07 advance was manual; the gap is not explained by the review-bot pause, which began 2026-09-11.
- Concretely: `rebar transition f920-dc37-28e4-4a91 in_progress closed` failed with 6 unmet criteria, each reporting the work absent from the tree. The verifier said so explicitly: "the current HEAD (665d1d0480...) does not contain these changes." The work was in fact merged and was the tip of `origin/main` at the time.

A second read-only investigation on 2026-09-19 confirmed the mechanism and corrected the remedy. The volume was fresh at that moment (`HEAD` = `origin/main` = `e900fa14ad52`, clean, ahead/behind `0 0`) — but **not because any mechanism refreshed it**. Its reflog carries out-of-band operations such as `reset: moving to origin/main`, which appear nowhere in the deployed scripts. Those are the manual break-glass fast-forwards. The freshness is entirely an artifact of somebody intervening.

## Impact

This silently corrupts the close and claim gates, which are the project's two certified operations.

- **False failures.** A ticket whose work has genuinely merged cannot be closed, because the verifier cannot see it. The failure text invites the operator to re-record evidence or to `--force`, and both responses are wrong — the evidence is real and the tree is stale. Agents are forbidden from using `--force`, so the correct-looking escape hatch is also unavailable, and the work simply cannot be closed.
- **False passes are possible in the other direction.** A criterion satisfied by code that has since been deleted or reworked on `main` still verifies against the frozen tree.
- The drift is unbounded and grows silently. Nothing reports it, and the gate output attributes the failure to the ticket rather than to the workspace.

## The two read modes, and why only one of them is broken

The workspace is a normal `main` working tree, not a bare repo. The gates read it two different ways, and the distinction decides what a refresh must actually do.

**Mode A — attested gate operations against a resolved ref.** These default to `origin/main`, materialize an immutable snapshot, and serve every file read from that snapshot rather than from the mutable checkout (`src/rebar/llm/gate_source.py:112-156`, `188-245`; `src/rebar/_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py:184-230`, `402-429`). For this path a `git fetch` alone suffices, because only the object database and the tracking ref need to advance. This mode is comparatively self-limiting.

**Mode B — close and op-cert completion paths.** These resolve `HEAD` explicitly with `fetch=False`, pinning whatever the persistent working tree currently points at (`src/rebar/_commands/close_autoresume.py:259-279`; `src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py:128-143`, `310-323`; `src/rebar/opcert_service/jobs.py:176-187`). A fetch is **not** enough here: the working-tree branch must actually be fast-forwarded, because `resolve_ref("HEAD", fetch=False)` and the later drift checks both read that same local `HEAD`. This is the mode that produces the false failures, and its staleness is unbounded by the deployed code.

Nothing refreshes Mode B incidentally. A container restart does not: the entrypoint returns as soon as `HEAD` resolves (`mcp-entrypoint.sh:175-177`). An image redeploy does not: `autodeploy.sh` fetches its own separate mirror at `/var/lib/rebar/mirror` (`autodeploy.sh:536-540`), mounts the pre-existing volume unchanged (`390-417`), and rolls containers without touching `MCP_CODE_DIR` (`852-920`, `948-960`).

## Approach

**Put the correctness boundary on the gate operation, not on the deploy tick.** An earlier draft of this plan proposed refreshing from `autodeploy.sh`, which runs on a timer. That bounds drift to one tick but does not make a gate fresh at the moment it runs, and it leaves correctness depending on a deploy cadence that a different deployment may not have at all. Deploy-path and entrypoint refreshes are worth keeping as a warm-up, but they must not be the thing the gate's correctness rests on.

- Add a reusable workspace-refresh helper and invoke it as a freshness boundary before a certified gate resolves a `HEAD`-based attested ref. It acquires the existing checkout lock, verifies the working tree is clean, runs `git fetch origin main`, then `git merge --ff-only origin/main`.
- The fetch needs a bounded retry window, because Gerrit's mirror replication to GitHub takes 20-25 seconds after a submit. A gate fired immediately on a merge can legitimately find the mirror not yet carrying the commit, and that is a wait, not a failure.
- **Fail closed and loudly.** If the remote is unreachable, if the retry budget is exhausted with the target still absent, if the tree is dirty, or if a fast-forward is impossible, the gate refuses and emits no signature. It must never fall back to verifying the stale tree — that is this bug reproduced inside its own fix. Diagnostics report the workspace `HEAD`, the target ref, the failure class, and whether the checkout was dirty or diverged.
- A dirty or diverged workspace is never mutated. Silently resetting a workspace a gate may be mid-read on trades one correctness bug for another, and it matches the existing `declared-service-down; decision=fail-loud-no-auto-restart` posture.

**Portability.** The trigger is the gate operation itself, plus optionally the MCP server lifecycle. That holds under GitHub Actions, under Gerrit, under another CI provider, and under no CI provider at all. A GitHub Actions workflow or a Gerrit hook as the *only* trigger would fail the blocking `project.portability` criterion, because the gate can still be invoked in an environment that has neither.

## Scope

- A reusable workspace-refresh helper: clean check, fetch with bounded retry, `merge --ff-only`, loud typed refusal.
- The gate seam that invokes it before resolving a `HEAD`-based attested ref, covering the Mode B call sites cited above.
- `infra/scripts/mcp-entrypoint.sh` — fetch and fast-forward an existing valid `MCP_CODE_DIR` as a warm-up, instead of only re-cloning a broken one.
- `infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md` — document the workspace, how to check its drift, and the manual fast-forward as the break-glass.

## Testing strategy

TDD, failing test first in each case.

1. A clean `MCP_CODE_DIR` behind `origin/main` fails today, because `mcp-entrypoint.sh --provision-only` returns early and leaves `HEAD` old; it passes once the helper fast-forwards.
2. Dirty and diverged checkouts assert **no mutation** and a loud typed failure.
3. A missing checkout, and one whose `HEAD` does not resolve, preserve today's re-clone behaviour.
4. A gate-seam test builds a local repo whose `HEAD` is behind `origin/main`, invokes the refresh boundary with no LLM call, and asserts `resolve_ref("HEAD", fetch=False)` sees the advanced SHA afterwards.
5. A mirror-lag test simulates the target SHA appearing only on a later fetch attempt and asserts the gate waits rather than refusing.
6. A retry-exhaustion test asserts the gate refuses and emits no signature, rather than verifying against the old `HEAD`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A certified gate invoked against a workspace behind `origin/main` verifies the advanced tree, not the stale one. Verified by a test that places `HEAD` behind the remote and asserts the resolved SHA after the refresh boundary runs.
- [ ] An existing, clean `MCP_CODE_DIR` that is behind `origin/main` is fast-forwarded rather than left frozen. Verified by that test failing against today's early-return provisioning.
- [ ] A dirty or diverged workspace is not mutated and the condition is reported loudly. Verified by asserting the working tree is byte-identical after the refusal and that the failure names the condition.
- [ ] A missing workspace, or one whose `HEAD` does not resolve, is still re-cloned exactly as today. Verified by a test covering both shapes.
- [ ] A fetch that cannot reach the target within the retry budget causes the gate to refuse and emit no signature. Verified by a test asserting no signature is produced and the stale tree is not verified.
- [ ] A target SHA that appears only after the mirror's 20-25 second replication lag is waited for rather than refused. Verified by a test where the fetch succeeds on a later attempt.
- [ ] The refresh trigger is the gate operation and the server lifecycle, with no dependency on any single CI provider. Verified by reading the trigger path and confirming no GitHub Actions or Gerrit hook is required for correctness.
- [ ] Drift is observable: the refresh emits the workspace SHA and its distance from the target. Verified by reading the emitted diagnostics.
- [ ] `infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md` documents the workspace, the drift check, and the manual fast-forward break-glass. Verified by reading the file.

## Out of scope

Changing Mode A's snapshot resolution, which already fetches. Any change to the certified gates' verdict logic. The separate `/var/lib/rebar/mirror` used by `autodeploy.sh`.

## Interim state

The workspace has been fast-forwarded by hand repeatedly to unblock closes, most recently to `e900fa14ad5`. That is a manual mitigation of a single symptom, not a fix: with nothing automated, it freezes again at whatever commit was current when the last person happened to intervene.
